notes.title: Puzzles of the Week are here!
notes.content:
The latest update to Replicube adds a new Puzzles of the Week feature!

New puzzles are now being added on a weekly basis!

Every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday a new puzzle is released. Check the new Puzzles of the Week section of FILES MANAGER for the latest puzzle.

The latest puzzle is always the 'active' puzzle (highlighted), and the leaderboards for that puzzle are live until the next puzzle is released.

Older puzzles are considered 'archived': you can still solve them, but the leaderboards are frozen (no new scores allowed).

Other players' solutions can be viewed (for archived leaderboards) by opening up the leaderboard and selecting the 'CODE VIEW' button.

Looking at other players' solutions is a great way to learn!

notes.title: RepliFest Summer 2025!
notes.content:
Our first official community event "RepliFest Summer 2025" is happening this Sunday, May 25th at 10am pacific!

This will be a live broadcast on my twitch channel (https://twitch.tv/walaber) featuring:

- Blind Speed Solve Tournament: contestants will have 10 minutes to solve never-before-seen puzzles, with points for solving first + having best code size / cycles scores at the end of the 10 minutes.

- Build Battle: contestants will have 10 minutes to create brand-new artwork based on a prompt, with twitch chat voting on the winner(s) of each round.

I hope to see you there!
-Walaber

-- EDIT --
The event was a great success!  if you missed it, the recording is now up on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fvvcb1OmLmk

notes.title: Performance improvements, Free Edit usability
notes.content:
This is a small update (1.1.1 Version 18C) that has a few changes:
[list]
[*] Switched RepliCube to multi-threaded execution to speed up evaluating large objects / animated objects.
[*] You can now have as many code tabs as you want in Free Edit mode to have multiple in-progress projects as you want.
[/list]

notes.title: Autocomplete improvements
notes.content: Version 1.1.1 / 17C is now live on Steam and makes some improvements to the code autocomplete system that should make it more useful for players.

notes.title: Rivals and Emojis are here!
notes.content:
A new update is now available on Steam (1.1.1 Version 17B) which has 2 major new features:

[h2]Rivals List[/h2]
you can now make a list of players (called your "rivals") and then filter all leaderboards to only show those players!  This should make the leaderboards a bit more meaningful for a wider range of players, or friend groups who are playing the game and want to easily compare their scores.

[h2]EMOJIS![/h2]
When posting in cubenet, we now have some beautiful 16x16 pixel art emojis that you can use!  See the new emoji panel on the right when posting, and click on an emoji to insert its name into your post.  In addition to many standard emojis, there are some fun ones specific to Cubenet.

[h2]Read Status[/h2]
Threads will now indicate if they have unread posts to help you keep track of what's new in cubenet.

notes.title: Version v1.1.1 (16B) is now available
notes.content:
Hello Replicubers!

The first post-release patch is now live on Steam.  This update mostly addresses bugs, but also has some new features.  Here's a short recap of the changes:

[olist]
[*] Added autocomplete to the code editor! It only knows about Lua keywords and built-in functions right now, autocompete for user variables or defined functions will come in a future update.
[*] Replipaint is now using multiple threads for a performance improvement
[*] Several improvements to how the game communicates with cubenet
[*] Fixed a few exploits with the token counting (code size) system
[*] when viewing a leaderboard, the game will now jump to your score first
[*] improved documentation formatting
[/olist]

I will be sharing my roadmap soon with my plan for future updates and improvements to the game as well, both in-game on cubenet, and here on Steam in the discussion forums.

Happy cubing!

notes.title: Replicube is an open-ended programming puzzle game about making 3D voxels
notes.content:
Walaber Entertainment LLC (JellyCar Worlds, Parking Garage Rally Circuit) have just released Replicube, an open-ended programming puzzle game where you make 3D voxel-based objects.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/04/replicube-is-an-open-ended-programming-puzzle-game-about-making-3d-voxels/
